facts.statement: Krabisuchus had a short and blunt snout where the rostrum was approximately as long as the back of the head from the eyesockets.

facts.statement: The skull of Krabisuchus is described as relatively deep, a condition known as altirostry.

facts.statement: The nasal bones of Krabisuchus are very wide, making up one-third of the maximum snout width.

facts.statement: Krabisuchus had large eyes and a small skull table located much higher than the snout.
facts.quote: The eyes of Krabisuchus were large and the small skull table is located much higher than the snout

facts.statement: Unlike in Procaimanoidea and Arambourgia, the outer edges of the squamosals in Krabisuchus run almost parallel, making the skull table more rectangular than trapezoid.
facts.quote: Unlike in Procaimanoidea and Arambourgia, the outer edges of the squamosals run almost parallel to each other, meaning that the structure as a whole is more rectangular than trapezoid

facts.statement: The affinities of the clade Orientalosuchina are disputed.

facts.statement: Tobias Massonne and his team argued that features initially interpreted as sutures in Krabisuchus were actually pre-orbital ridges.
facts.quote: However, Tobias Massonne and his team later argued that what were initially interpreted as sutures between skull bones actually represented pre-orbital ridges similar to those seen in Orientalosuchus and modern saltwater crocodiles

facts.statement: The underside of the Krabisuchus skull has a small incisive foramen and two suborbital openings that are smaller than the eye sockets.
facts.quote: The underside of the skull features a small incisive foramen and two suborbital fenestrae that are slightly wider than long and overall smaller than the eyesockets.

facts.statement: One specimen shows that Krabisuchus had five teeth in each of the front upper jaw bones.

facts.statement: The rear teeth of Krabisuchus were low-crowned and bulbous in shape.
facts.quote: The teeth further back in the jaw meanwhile have been described as low crowned and bulbous.

facts.statement: The teeth of Krabisuchus were arranged in an overbite where lower teeth slid into pits behind the upper teeth.
facts.quote: Overall, the teeth of Krabisuchus appear to have been arranged in an overbite, with the teeth of the lower jaw sliding into occlusal pits that sit lingual to the teeth of the upper jaw.

facts.statement: Krabisuchus had at least two types of bony armor, including square-shaped plates with a concave underside likely forming the back armor.
facts.quote: At least two osteoderm types could be identified, the first of which consisting of square-shaped keeled osteoderms with a moderately concave underside that likely belonged to the dorsal armor.

facts.statement: The back armor of Krabisuchus likely consisted of multiple rows of overlapping plates.
facts.quote: The osteoderms feature articular surfaces on two sides, which for one suggests that the dorsal armor would have consisted of multiple rows in articulation with one another.

facts.statement: The neck armor plates of Krabisuchus overlapped each other but did not form continuous rows along the body length.
facts.quote: At the same time, such surfaces are absent in the front and back, which indicates that they did not articulate down the length of the body but instead each osteoderm overlapped the one behind it.

facts.quote: Krabisuchus was a small alligatoroid growing no larger than 2 m in length, making it smaller than modern American alligators.

facts.statement: The fossil-bearing sediments of the Krabi Basin consist of ancient river deposits, a primary coal seam, and overlying lake deposits.
